turns.t: Morning, doctor. I'm Rosa, I'm Mr Quinn's carer, and this is his son, Danny. We're worried about his tiredness and his skin.
Hello Rosa, hello Danny, hello Mr Quinn. Tell me what you've noticed. ~
I'm fine. A bit tired, that's all.
He's more than a bit tired, Dad. He's been exhausted for months, and his skin is going dark, especially his hands, and around his elbows.
Mr Quinn, when did the tiredness start?
Oh, I couldn't say, I've been slow for a while.
And the darker skin, did you notice it, when did it begin?
I haven't noticed it. Danny's the one who points it out. I couldn't tell you when.
I noticed it in the spring, in his palm creases, but I'm not sure when exactly.
I'll note that none of you can pin it down. Mr Quinn, any dizziness, especially when you stand up?
No. No dizziness.
He does get dizzy, doctor. He held the wall twice last week, getting up from the chair.
And he nearly fell in the bathroom.
I'll record that Mr Quinn says no, and Rosa and Danny say yes. What medicines does he take?
Just the hydrocortisone, 10 mg in the morning and 5 mg in the afternoon, but I'm not sure he's been taking the afternoon dose.
Hydrocortisone, for what condition?
Addison's disease, diagnosed ten years ago.
And is there anything else?
Underactive thyroid too.
Mr Quinn, are you taking your hydrocortisone? ~
Mostly. I forget the afternoon ones, I'm sure. ~
I'll check. Is there any vomiting, diarrhoea, or weight loss? ~
A bit of nausea. Nothing else. ~
Let me check his chest and pulse, and I'd like to check his blood pressure sitting and standing. ~
He's quite wobbly on his feet. ~
Right. Because of the possible dizziness, the dark skin, and the missed doses, I'd say this looks like his Addison's disease is under-treated, an adrenal problem.
Is that dangerous? ~
It can be, if it gets worse, because a low steroid level can cause a crisis. I'd like to arrange blood tests today, to check his sodium, potassium and cortisol.
We can do it now? ~
Yes. Please make sure he takes his hydrocortisone, including the afternoon dose, and use a pill box.
I'll set the alarms. ~
And if he's vomiting, very dizzy, confused, or collapses, take him straight to the emergency department, and tell them he has Addison's.
I carry a steroid card. ~
Good. I'd like to see you again in a week.
We'll be there. ~

clinical_uncertainties.description: Neither the patient nor his carer could say when the tiredness and skin darkening began.
Patient says he has no dizziness; his carer and son say he gets dizzy and nearly fell (unresolved).

clinical_actions.description: Take all hydrocortisone doses including the afternoon dose; use a pill box and alarms
Emergency department immediately if vomiting, very dizzy, confused or collapse; tell them he has Addison's

contradictions_detected: Patient denies dizziness; caregiver and family member report he gets dizzy on standing (unresolved).
